questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas at a pressure of $2 \mathrm{~atm}$ is heated from $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $323^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and simultaneously compressed of $\frac{2}{3}$ rd of its original value. Then the final pressure is
questions.solution:
Given, $p_1=2 \mathrm{~atm}\begin{aligned} p_2 & =? \\ V_1 & =1 \mathrm{~L} \\ V_2 & =\frac{3}{2} \\ T_1 & =298 \mathrm{~K} \\ T_2 & =596 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$
Using combined gas law, we get
$\begin{aligned} \frac{p_1 V_1}{T_1} & =\frac{p_2 V_2}{T_2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad p_2 & =\frac{2 \times 1}{298} \times \frac{3 \times 596}{2}=6 \mathrm{~atm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
The volume of $2.8 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{CO}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and 0.821 atm pressure is

\left(R=0.08210 \text { L. atm K }{ }^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}\right)
questions.solution:
Given, amount of $\mathrm{CO}=2.8 \mathrm{~g}$
Temperature $=27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
Pressure $=0.821 \mathrm{~atm}R=0.08210 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~K}{ }^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
We know that, $p V=R T\therefore \quad V=\frac{R T}{p}=\frac{0.0821 \times 300}{0.821}=30 \mathrm{~L}\therefore 28 \mathrm{~g}$ of CO occupy volume $30 \mathrm{~L}\therefore 2.8 \mathrm{~g}$ of CO occupy volume $=\frac{30 \times 2.8}{28}=3 \mathrm{~L}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the absolute temperature of ideal gas is doubled and pressure is halved, the volume of gas
options: will be half of original volume
will be 4 times the original volume
will be 2 times the original volume
will be $1 / 4$ th times the original volume
questions.solution:
Given, final temperature $\left(T_{2}\right)=2 \times\left(T_{1}\right)$ initial temperatue Final pressure $\left(p_{2}\right)=2 \times \frac{\left(p_{1}\right)}{2}$ initial pressure
According to gas law,
$\frac{p_{1} V_{1}}{T_{1}}=\frac{p_{2} V_{2}}{T_{2}}\therefore \quad \frac{p_{1} V_{1}}{T_{1}}=\frac{p_{1} \times V_{2}}{2 \times 2 T_{1}}V_{2}=4 V_{1}\therefore$ Volume increase by 4 times.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas mixture contains $25 \%$ He and $75 \% \mathrm{CH}_{4}$ by volume at a given temperature and pressure. The percentage by mass of methane in the mixture is approximately____
questions.solution:
Gas mixture contains $25 \%$ He and $75 \% \mathrm{CH}_{4}$ by volumes. We have to calculate the mass percentage of methane in the mixture.
molar mass of $\mathrm{He}=4$
molar mass of $\mathrm{CH}_{4}=16\therefore$ Mass percentage of methane in the mixture shall be $=\frac{75 \times 16}{25 \times 4+75 \times 16} \times 100=92 \%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gases has the highest value of RMS velocity at $298 \mathrm{~K}$ ?
questions.solution:
RMS-velocity of a gas $v_{\text {rms }}=\sqrt{\frac{3 R T}{M}}$
Hence, higher the molecular weigth of a gas, lower will be its RMS-velocity
$v_{\text {rms }} \propto \sqrt{\frac{1}{M}}\therefore \mathrm{CH}_{4}$ (mol. weight $=16$ ) has highest RMS-velocity.

2-2 x & x

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $0.5$ mole of each of $\mathrm{H}_{2}, \mathrm{SO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CH}_{4}$ are kept in a container. A hole was made in the container. After $3 \mathrm{~h}$, the order of partial pressures in the container will be
questions.solution:
Rate of diffusion $\propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\text { molecular mass }}}\therefore$ Order of diffusion $: \mathrm{H}_{2}\gt \mathrm{CH}_{4}\gt \mathrm{SO}_{2}$ and amount left is in the order $\mathrm{SO}_{2}\gt \mathrm{CH}_{4}\gt \mathrm{H}_{2}$ Hence, order of partial pressure is

\mathrm{pSO}_{2}>\mathrm{pCH}_{4}>\mathrm{pH}_{2}

questions.q: A gas deviates from ideal behaviour at a high pressure because its molecules
questions.solution: At high pressure, the volume is decreased appreciably, so the attractive forces become large and the molecules are crowded together. Thus, pressure correction is necessary and the gas deviates more from ideal behaviour.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Dalton's law of partial pressure is applicable to which one of the following systems?
questions.solution: When a mixture of two or more non-reacting gases are enclosed in a container then the total pressure exerted by the gaseous mixture is equal to the sum of partial pressure of the components in the mixture. e.g. $\mathrm{CO}+\mathrm{H}_{2}$ are non-reacting gases. Hence, Dalton's law of partial pressure is applicable to this system.
